newsitem.title: UK: Lowndes Lambert, Fenchurch to merge.
newsitem.headline: Lowndes Lambert, Fenchurch to merge.

text.p: Two major British insurance brokers Lowndes Lambert Group Holdings Plc and Fenchurch Plc said on Thursday that they have decided to merge their operations to form a new company to be called the Lambert Fenchurch Group.
Lowndes Lambert would make a merger offer for all of Fenchurch shares, the two firms said in a joint statement.
Fenchurch shareholders will be offered 628 new Lambert Fenchurch shares for every 1,000 Fenchurch shares, they said

The merger of the two brokers is the latest evidence of consolidation in the UK insurance industry, which has been hit by declining premiums and a fall in margins, forcing many players to reduce costs.
The merger is expected to save at least 5.0 million pounds ($8.4 million) before tax for both firms.
After the merger, Lowndes Lambert shareholders would hold approximately 72 percent in the new group while Fenchurch shareholders would control 28 percent.
The merger offer values Fenchurch's issued and to be issued share capital at about 27.6 million pounds. At this price Lowndes Lambert's market capitalisation has been pegged at 67.3 million.

"The boards of both Lowndes Lambert and Fenchurch will be unanimously recommending that their respective shareholders take such steps as are necessary to implement the merger," both firms said in the joint statement.
